notes: 39/39 tests, 69/69 assertions, port:parity --complete clean. All five jsdom stubs deleted. GAINED is the thesis: real layout + real ResizeObserver cover shared/useSize.ts L19-48, SliderThumbImpl.vue L40 (getThumbInBoundsOffset only runs once the thumb has a measured size) and Slider/utils.ts L67-70,L110-111. The single LOST line is itself a finding — see #linear-scale-degenerate. Two structural deviations, both recorded below: #form-submit-button and #home-end-name.

QUARANTINED via it.fails — reported, not fixed. The jsdom axe test is vacuous: Slider.test.ts:27-33 calls axe(wrapper.element) synchronously after mount(), before Vue flushes, so the thumb still carries display:none from SliderThumbImpl.vue:80 (the SSR anti-jank branch, active while value === undefined). axe skips hidden elements, so aria-input-field-name comes back INAPPLICABLE and the only interactive element in the component is never audited. await render() flushes, axe sees the thumb, and reports a real violation: single-thumb sliders have no accessible name because getLabel (utils.ts:35) only auto-labels 2+ thumbs and the story fixture supplies none. The gap is in the fixture, not the library. Not strictly a jsdom-vs-browser difference — jsdom reports it too once flushed (verified experimentally) — but browser mode is what surfaced it. Resolve by giving _Slider.vue an aria-label, NOT by disabling the rule.

The only line the browser port fails to cover is Slider/utils.ts:109 — linearScale's `if (input[0] === input[1]) return output[0]` short-circuit. jsdom takes that branch on EVERY pointer test, because the slider measures 0x0 so `rect.width - thumbWidth` is 0; the browser takes L110-111, the real interpolation, instead. So a line the jsdom suite reports as covered was only ever covered by the absence of layout, and the arithmetic the component actually ships was never executed. This is the coverage-parity oracle's first justified LOST line; exempted via PORT-COVERAGE-ALLOW.tsv, which is machine-checked against this file. Generalises: coverage lost to a port is not automatically a regression, but it must be argued line by line.

The jsdom form block fires a synthetic `submit` on the <form>, which no user can do. Ported with a real <button type="submit"> (see AGENTS.md 'Settled questions' — implicit submission via Enter on the focused thumb does NOT submit this form, 0 calls, and neither suite would have caught that). Also: vitest-browser-vue unmounts after every test, so the component is rendered per test in a beforeEach rather than once at describe-body level as the original does. The module-level handleSubmit spy still accumulates calls across tests, so the original's 1-then-2 call-count assertions port unchanged.

Naming bug in the jsdom original, carried over verbatim: under 'when vertical > when inverted', `it('home should set value to 100')` asserts 0 and `it('end should set value to 0')` asserts 100. The assertions are right — Home/End are semantic (min/max) per ARIA APG and ignore `inverted` by design — and the names are simply wrong. PORTING.md rule 4 says to fix the test so the name becomes true, but applying it here would fail a component that is behaving correctly, so the assertions were kept and the deviation recorded here. Browser mode contributed nothing to finding this; reading the file did.

MUTATION-VERIFIED (PORTING.md 2.3), the T3 thesis proved rather than asserted. Deleting `target.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)` from SliderImpl.vue's pointerdown handler — i.e. breaking pointer capture outright — makes the browser port's 'should emit valueCommit on wrapper' FAIL and leaves the jsdom test PASSING. jsdom passes because its own mock, `hasPointerCapture: vi.fn().mockImplementation(id => id)`, answers yes for a capture that was never taken, so pointerup still emits slideEnd. The jsdom test cannot fail this mutation by construction. Source reverted immediately; verified with git diff.
